lines.text: The next morning, heralds read the Tourney rules in every square in Aldcrown. Most of it was about horses. One line wasn't.
And the champion of the King's Tourney may ask one boon of His Majesty, as King Aldric granted boons of old. And His Majesty shall grant it.
One boon. Anything. A title. A fortune. A pardon. Or a Royal Ward's freedom, and his seat, and his name back on the Compact.
Then I'll win it.
So will I.
You can't both win.
Watch me.
There was one problem. A commoner can only enter the Tourney under a lord's name. And I wasn't a lord any more. I was a ward. I couldn't have sponsored a goat.
So Wren walked into the palace yard, where the princess was training, and asked.
Put my name on them. Both of them. I want my rematch, archer. In front of the whole city, this time.
In front of the whole city, Highness. I'll try not to embarrass you.
Try harder than last time.

That night, the lists went up outside the cathedral. Lords from every corner of the kingdom. Sir Oswin Hale, under the Princess's name. Wren of Greyhollow, under the Princess's name. Lord Roderick Stane.
And at the very bottom, in fresh ink, one more.
Brother Caddoc. For the Order.
Good.
Good.
So my friends would fight for me. And I couldn't fight for anyone. I never had been able to. I could only do one thing.
The next morning, Holt walked me down to the Lowmarket. I borrowed a shovel from Mags, climbed to the foot of the broken arch, and started to dig.
You're mad, zero. One man can't mend an aqueduct.
No. But one man can start.
By noon, Holt had taken off his tabard and was carrying stones. By afternoon, Mags had brought her cousins. By sunset, there were forty of us. Not one thread between us. Not yet.
My hands were still black from the Stone. Every shovelful hurt. It was the best I had felt since I came south.
And high above us, in the tallest window of the cathedral, a man in white watched us dig until dark.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter eighty-three, coming soon.
